mandatory_decision_gate.method: Independent, three-part audit performed before any code was touched: (1) static line-by-line read of src/data_pipeline/lexical_outlierness.py and src/data_pipeline/lexical_outlierness_pilot.py against logs/3d_a_lexical_outlierness_design.md sections 2, 3, 4, 6; (2) fresh from-scratch manual re-derivation of the S2 IDF/centroid/cosine construction and the S3 count/N/|V|/self-information construction, diffed numerically against the module's own functions on a synthetic fold (see reproducibility.manual_rederivation_check below); (3) full pilot re-run from an unmodified checkout, in a scratch copy of the repository so the frozen 3D-B artifacts were never touched, to confirm bit-for-bit reproducibility.

s2_checklist.raw_within_document_tf_counts: MATCH - word_ngrams_1_2() builds a Counter of raw n-gram occurrence counts; _vectorize() multiplies count*idf directly with no augmentation or log scaling.
s2_checklist.group_local_idf: MATCH - fold_tfidf() computes df/idf only from ref_feats, which the caller (run_pilot's per-group loop) has already restricted to rows outside the held-out group (`ref_ids = [rid for rid in record_ids if rid not in members]`).
s2_checklist.per_document_l2_normalization: MATCH - _vectorize() L2-normalizes each document's raw TF-IDF vector to unit length before it is used in centroid construction, exactly as S2 requires ('normalize-first step... applied identically to v_i and to every reference vector before centroid construction').
s2_checklist.cosine_distance_to_logo_centroid: MATCH - score_tfidf() returns 1 - cosine(v_i, mu_i); mu_i is the fold-local (LOGO) centroid; mu is not re-normalized after averaging, matching the design doc's explicit note that this is immaterial under cosine.
s2_checklist.idf_formula: MATCH - idf_{-g}(t) = ln((1+total_weight)/(1+df)) + 1, algebraically identical to the design doc's ln((1+|R_-g|)/(1+df_-g(t)))+1 for the unweighted (primary) case where total_weight == |R_-g|. Independently re-derived from scratch and diffed at 0.0 max absolute error against fold_tfidf()'s output on a synthetic 3-document fold.
s2_checklist.centroid_averaging_order: MATCH - mu_i = (1/|R_-g|) * sum(v_j_normalized), i.e. averaging happens strictly after per-document L2 normalization, matching the design doc's locked centroid construction. Independently re-derived and diffed at 0.0 max absolute error.

s3_checklist.repeated_token_occurrences: MATCH - score_selfinfo() sums over the token *list* (with repeats), not a deduplicated vocabulary set, matching 'the sum is over token occurrences in x_i, not over x_i's distinct vocabulary'.
s3_checklist.fixed_alpha_1_0: MATCH - module-level constant ALPHA = 1.0, used unconditionally in score_selfinfo().
s3_checklist.division_by_n_i: MATCH - score_selfinfo() divides the summed surprisal by len(tokens), and n_i is defined identically (len(tokens[rid])) wherever n_i is used elsewhere (length diagnostics, OOV diagnostic).
s3_checklist.count_and_normalizer_construction: MATCH - fold_selfinfo() builds c_{-g}(t) as raw token-occurrence counts over ref_tokens (LOGO-excluded), N_{-g} as their sum, and |V_{-g}| as the number of distinct types - independently re-derived from scratch and diffed as exactly equal (dict equality) against fold_selfinfo()'s output on the same synthetic fold used for the S2 check.

shared_checklist.held_out_group_exclusion_from_all_refere: MATCH - a single `ref_ids` computation (excluding the entire held-out group, not just the held-out row) feeds both fold_tfidf() and fold_selfinfo() for every fold in the per-group loop in lexical_outlierness_pilot.run_pilot().
shared_checklist.locked_preprocessing: MATCH - normalize_text() performs NFKC -> lowercase -> URL placeholder -> whitespace collapse/strip; tokenize() uses \b\w+\b; stopwords are never removed. Verified both by static read and by the pre-existing passing unit tests (test_normalize_text_url_and_whitespace, test_normalize_text_nfkc, test_tokenize_apostrophe_not_word_char, test_word_ngrams_1_2).
shared_checklist.exact_group_assignments: MATCH - re-running build_groups() on the exact 209-row population from a clean checkout reproduces data/quadrant_c_pipeline/lexical_outlierness_groups_v1.json byte-for-byte (SHA-256 9d5f14ae3597d5cd1c20d58aa194739be5c956beeaeda0b638b7f5d4a8ff0f39, identical to the committed, frozen artifact). The frozen artifact itself was not touched by this check (written only inside a scratch copy of the repository, then diffed and discarded).
shared_checklist.fold_calibrated_percentile_construction: MATCH - calibrated_percentile() implements the exact '<' + 0.5*'=' tie rule over the fold's reference-score distribution F_{g,m}; F_{g,m} itself is built by scoring every reference row directly against the fold's own fitted statistics (compute_fold_variant()'s ref_scores_tfidf / ref_scores_selfinfo), i.e. each reference row is NOT further leave-one-out'd within its own fold - exactly matching S6 step 3's explicit instruction ('not re-fit with itself excluded').

length_dependence_status: REMAINS. Unmitigated - by design, since no construct-preserving correction is justified.
why_no_correction_is_mathematically_avai: The design doc (Section 8 of this task's brief, and the S2 'immaterial to the score' note in logs/3d_a_lexical_outlierness_design.md) already identifies and forecloses the one length-normalization move that would otherwise seem obvious: dividing a document's raw TF-IDF vector by its token count before the prescribed L2 normalization is pure scalar rescaling and cancels exactly under cosine similarity, so it is not a distinct construct at all, merely a no-op wrapped in extra arithmetic. No other length adjustment is licensed by the locked S2/S3 definitions without changing what is being measured (sublinear TF, BM25, L1 norm, document-length penalties, and residualized/regression-adjusted primary scores are all explicitly excluded by this task's brief as redesigns, not corrections). The audit above confirms the length association is not an artifact of a coding error: it is what raw-count TF-IDF with (1,2)-gram features and cosine-to-centroid distance does on this population, most plausibly because longer prompts contribute proportionally more distinct, low-document-frequency bigrams (bigram counts grow faster than unigram counts with length, and are individually rarer), which pushes their L2-normalized vector further from a centroid dominated by shorter, more template-like prompts.
conclusion_statement: No construct-preserving correction is justified by the locked S2/S3 definitions; the observed length dependence remains a property of this exact operationalization and dataset.
